quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Listen closely to "pole". For /p/, you press both lips together and release with no voice — like the start of "pie". Does that match what you hear?
quests.explanation: "pole" features /p/ rather than /b/. /p/ comes from pressing both lips together and releasing with no voice, which is why it sounds distinct from the voiced bilabial plosive /b/ used in words like "boy".
quests.mouthPosition: Press both lips together and release with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: "ton" contains one of these two sounds. /t/ is a voiceless alveolar plosive, made when you tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice. /d/ is a voiced alveolar plosive instead.
quests.explanation: In "ton", the target sound is /t/, made by tapping your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice. The distractor /d/ would instead require you to tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with your voice on — a clearly different sound once you isolate it.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, tap your tongue tip on the ridge behind your top teeth with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Say "pig" slowly and isolate just the target consonant. To make /p/, you press both lips together and release with no voice. To make /b/, you press both lips together and release with your voice on. Which one are you actually doing?
quests.explanation: The word "pig" contains /p/, a voiceless bilabial plosive, made by pressing both lips together and releasing with no voice. It's easy to confuse with /b/, a voiced bilabial plosive, but the two are produced quite differently.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel it in the mouth: press both lips together and release with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD

quests.explanation: "pin" is a good example of /p/: you press both lips together and release with no voice. Compare that with /b/, where you'd instead press both lips together and release with your voice on — the two shouldn't be mixed up once you feel the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: Press both lips together and release with no voice.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE TARGET CONSONANT PHONEME IN THE WORD
quests.hint: Think about what your mouth is doing during the target sound in "cone". Does it raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice? Or does it raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with your voice on?
quests.explanation: The consonant in "cone" is /k/, not /g/. To produce /k/, you raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice; /g/ is made differently, by raising the back of your tongue to the soft palate with your voice on.
quests.mouthPosition: To produce this sound, raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate with no voice.
